hints.content: Let's start by finding the area of each small rectangle separately.

options.alt: An area model for a rectangle that has a height of x plus three and a width of x plus nine. The rectangle is broken into four rectangles to isolate each term in the height and the width. The top left rectangle has a height of x and a width of x. The area of the top left rectangle is x squared. The top right rectangle has a height of x and width of nine. The area of the top right rectangle is nine x. The bottom left rectangle has a height of three and a width of x. The area of the bottom left rectangle is three x. The bottom right rectangle has a height of three and a width of nine. The area of the bottom right rectangle is twenty-seven.

hints.content:
The area of the entire rectangle is the sum of those areas:

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}&=x^2+9x+3x+27
\\\\
&=x^2+12x+27
\end{align}$
